title: Consumption mode for a slice: take a named list of files from a pinned release of a repository into one that has its own files
note: Found 2026-11-17 by grenudi/ideal-knowledge-base (research chain-follow-world, decision 2026-11-17-chain-follow-by-slice). Its chain - idealkb to device-template to device bases - lays a slice, not a repository: a source names what it gives (a generic list, files whole or the part between two marker lines), a follower pins a release and names its own files, and the verdict says whether the follower changed a generic file (idealkb's bin/follow.sh ends 3). rhizoid today takes a whole fork (a cutting); this is the consumption side design-consumption-side leaves open. follow.sh and update-pins.sh are the prototype; when rhizoid has it, idealkb can hand its chain over. Also lacking for that chain: the pin read from the follower's own file, a release gate (every follower answers before a release is tagged), and sending a changed generic file back as a patch. Also 2026-11-17: the tools home (linux-phone-oco/lab-tools) has the same slice case for the device-template files that go with a tool - the [boot] manifest skeleton, hook examples, an initramfs skeleton - beside the tool's own version pin (see cutting-as-cargo-dependency, followers-one-pin-bump). Reshaped 2026-11-18 (docs research base-graph-measured, base-graph-world; decision 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs; upstream item rhizoid-scope-every-edge (linux-phone-oco/docs)): rhizoid's scope is the follow tool for every edge (slice, tool pin, cutting), built in order status-over-every-edge, follow-by-conformance, send-back, cuttings; each replaces shell only once it passes the shell's tests. Unparking implement-cli waits on the author's word.

title: A cutting consumed by a language manager: the patched fork of a Rust tool as a cargo git dependency at a pinned tag, written and bumped by rhizoid
note: Found 2026-11-17 by linux-phone-oco/docs (research bringup-home-follow-and-rhizoid, decision 2026-11-17-bringup-in-lab-tools). A device repository uses lab-tools' bringup as a pinned binary or cargo git dependency; when it must patch the tool itself before upstream takes the change, the true case is a cutting of lab-tools (tracking branch pristine, patch branch merged from it, clean patch back). What rhizoid lacks is the consumption side for it: the follower declares this tool, this cutting, this tag, and rhizoid writes the pin where the language manager reads it (Cargo.toml git tag or [patch] entry; a rust-script file's cargo header; a version line in a manifest) and bumps it when the tracking branch has a new release - the open item design-consumption-side, for a case that now has a user. Until then: a plain fork and a [patch] line by hand, recorded as a problem.

title: Many followers, one pin and one verdict: a slice, a cutting and a tool version bumped by the same weekly job
note: Found 2026-11-17 by linux-phone-oco/docs (same research). A device repository follows three sources - idealkb (a slice), device-template (a slice) and lab-tools (a tool version, maybe a cutting) - each with its own pin line, and today an updater (idealkb's update-pins.sh) only for the slices. Lacking: one pin file the follower owns (source, kind slice|cutting|tool, release), one command that bumps every pin to the newest release and opens a pull request per source, and one verdict (up to date, behind, own change to a generic file) that CI can gate on. update-pins.sh and follow.sh's exit 3 are the prototype; slice-consumption is the first kind. Reshaped 2026-11-18 (docs research base-graph-measured, base-graph-world; decision 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs; upstream item rhizoid-scope-every-edge (linux-phone-oco/docs)): rhizoid's scope is the follow tool for every edge (slice, tool pin, cutting), built in order status-over-every-edge, follow-by-conformance, send-back, cuttings; each replaces shell only once it passes the shell's tests. Unparking implement-cli waits on the author's word. Reshaped 2026-11-23 (decisions 2026-11-23-rhizoid-carries-the-structure-git-flows, 2026-11-23-structure-flows-ranked-first; linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid): every pin's status in one place (lab.toml lpoco, idealkb.toml, device-template slices, procedures' lpoco-attended pins); repo-only bumps as pull requests; a gated bump (--gate CMD, e.g. lpoco-attended check) for attended pins; lab.toml lpoco: rhizoid bumps the pin, lpoco-host follow installs. Not Renovate.

title: Sending a change back: a patch to the source as a pull request, and the follower's own record of it
note: Found 2026-11-17 by linux-phone-oco/docs (same research). clean-patch-back says a diff of the patch branch against the pristine tracking branch is a clean patch; the CLI that makes it and opens the pull request is stubbed. The follower's bases keep an upstream item per change (idealkb: ikb upstream-item, form patch, draft, ready on the person's word, sent with the PR address, landed when released). Lacking: a rhizoid verb that, for a changed generic file or a patch branch, writes the patch, opens the pull request only after the person says ready, and returns the PR address and later the release that carried it, in a form the follower's record command takes - without rhizoid knowing that base's tables. It never sends in the person's name by itself. Reshaped 2026-11-18 (docs research base-graph-measured, base-graph-world; decision 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs; upstream item rhizoid-scope-every-edge (linux-phone-oco/docs)): rhizoid's scope is the follow tool for every edge (slice, tool pin, cutting), built in order status-over-every-edge, follow-by-conformance, send-back, cuttings; each replaces shell only once it passes the shell's tests. Unparking implement-cli waits on the author's word. Reshaped 2026-11-23 (decisions 2026-11-23-rhizoid-carries-the-structure-git-flows, 2026-11-23-structure-flows-ranked-first; linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid): rebase topic/ITEM onto the target tree onto send/ITEM/vN (stop naming the commit at a conflict); format-patch --cover-letter -vN --base into the folder given (upstream/LIST/ITEM/vN-draft/); range-diff vs topic/ITEM/vN-1; a changelog skeleton from it; --base and the tested commit (passed in, never guessed) for SEND-NOTES; get_maintainer.pl recipients; checkpatch --strict stops it (a missing SoB and an unresolvable Fixes listed, not hidden); W=1 / dt-check as a check command by exit code. Out: signing, re-authoring, send-email, pushing, lore, b4, claims in the cover letter.

title: rhizoid status: one read-only report over every edge a repository has - a slice (pin vs source release, followed files equal, own files on their way up), a tool pin (vs latest tag), a cutting (tracking vs upstream head) - exit 1 on drift
note: Found 2026-11-18 by linux-phone-oco (docs research base-graph-measured, base-graph-world; decision 2026-11-18-device-layer-from-docs; upstream item rhizoid-scope-every-edge (linux-phone-oco/docs)). The first command to build: no risk, it replaces docs' graph-drift.sh (36 FAIL today) and passes it line for line. Edges are read from the pin files followers already own (idealkb.toml, devicebase.toml, lab.toml [tools], a fork's .rhizoid/module.toml), so the follower lists derive from the pins. Rust with argenv, the CLI's status command. Unparked 2026-11-18 (see implement-cli): first in the author's order. Built in rhizoid-cli: status reads a graph file of the edges and each follower's own pin files at origin/main, reports every edge current, behind or moved by hand, exits 1 on drift, and is proven by graph-drift.sh's cases as fixtures and by agreeing with graph-drift.sh run on the real graph. Released 2026-11-18 as git-rhizoid/rhizoid v0.1.0 (PRs 7, 8, 9): rhizoid status over a graph file (examples/linux-phone-oco.graph.toml: slice, device layer, tool pin, fork), agreeing with graph-drift.sh edge by edge on the real graph (tests/agree-with-graph-drift.sh). The graph file exists because idealkb.toml names no source: when pins name theirs (follow-by-conformance, rule one), the follower lists derive from the pins and the file shrinks to what pins cannot say. The graph file for the real graph belongs in linux-phone-oco/docs, whose owner keeps graph-drift.sh. Next: follow-by-conformance.

title: rhizoid assemble: a named list of branches merged onto a fresh base in a worktree, rerere shared, stopped at a conflict naming both, tagged int/DEVICE/LIST/BASE/N
note: List format owned by rhizoid (TOML; named lists [lists.NAME]; base a tag or a fork commit; entries in order, each a topic/ITEM or backport/ITEM/BASE branch with for and state = known-good (test_run, tested_commit) or trying); a fresh worktree each time in the home, git merge with rerere.enabled + autoUpdate; at a conflict it stops and names the entry and the earlier entry that touched the same paths; an annotated tag with the base and every sha; --reproduces COMMIT compares TAG^{tree} with the commit's tree (surya: 29d92793b); several assembled worktrees alive at once, locked while wanted (walleye); output key=value and --json for the caller's record command (fields: ikb's answer pending). Proof: a fixture repository - two topics assemble to a tag holding both; a conflict stops naming both; reproduces says equal and says which paths differ; a worktree outside the home is refused. Decisions 2026-11-23-rhizoid-carries-the-structure-git-flows, 2026-11-23-standard-tools-drive-cut-or-write; linux-phone-oco/docs decision 2026-11-23-structure-git-flows-run-on-rhizoid.
